free_tier.stated: AI Free: USD 0 with unlimited AI completion in JetBrains IDEs and 3 AI credits every 30 days, one AI credit being USD 1.00 of AI use, with no top-up and no rollover; paid plans are AI Pro, USD 100 a year for 10 credits every 30 days, and AI Ultimate, USD 300 a year for 35 credits every 30 days
free_tier.notes: credits are spent at the model vendor's public API rate, so the number of tasks that 3 credits buy depends on the agent and model; the page publishes no credits-per-task figure

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a subscription meters AI use, not objects

record.interface_detail: Junie CLI (junie, Linux, macOS and Windows) runs interactively and headless; Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie also run in the AI chat of a JetBrains IDE and in the JetBrains Air app; JetBrains Central CLI connects Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie CLI to the JetBrains AI subscription from a terminal
record.tooling: the user installs Junie CLI with a curl or PowerShell install script, or a JetBrains IDE with the AI Assistant plugin, or JetBrains Central CLI; AI Free is offered in JetBrains IDEs except Android Studio, IntelliJ IDEA without Ultimate and PyCharm without Pro
record.chaining: Junie CLI headless takes a Junie API key (usage-based billing) with --auth or a licence key with --auth-license, and JetBrains Central CLI routes Claude Agent, Codex and Gemini CLI to the JetBrains AI subscription and offers service accounts for headless and CI use; whether an AI Free or AI Pro licence qualifies for Central CLI access is not stated. Bring-your-own-key and provider-account routes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot) bypass JetBrains credits and bill the provider

limits.value: AI Free 3 AI credits every 30 days, AI Pro 10, AI Ultimate 35; one AI credit is USD 1.00 of AI use; unused credits do not roll over; top-up credits (AI Pro and AI Ultimate only) stay valid 12 months

record.limits_note: AI Free has no top-up, so it ends at 3 credits a month
record.binding_note: the monthly AI credit allowance is the cap on every plan, and on AI Free it is 3 credits

identity_cost.detail: a JetBrains Account, created with an email address (one-time code, name and password) or a third-party login; JetBrains AI support says AI Free and AI Trial sign-up sometimes asks to link a payment card as a verification step with no charge, and the AI Pro trial asks to link a payment card; whether a card is asked for AI Free today is unverified: behind a sign-up, since the support article on it was last updated over a year before the read; AI Free is offered only in serviceable territories and inside a JetBrains IDE

record.reliability_note: the JetBrains AI service stopped serving China on 2026-07-13, and Junie CLI headless mode is described on its own page as an early access program
record.confidence_note: plans, credit counts, prices, agents, headless flags, sign-up steps and the card step are quoted from first-party pages read on 2026-11-02; Junie's JetBrains-account login in headless mode, Central CLI access for an AI Free licence, credits per task, and the current AI Free card prompt are unverified

record.notes: compute/jetbrains-student-pack records the student and teacher route, which is verification-gated; this record is the AI Free plan, which needs no institution. One AI credit is USD 1.00 of AI use billed at public API rates, so the free plan buys USD 3.00 of model use every 30 days and inline completion is the durable free part. AI Free is not offered in IntelliJ IDEA without an Ultimate subscription, in PyCharm without a Pro subscription, or in Android Studio, so the free plan needs one of the other JetBrains IDEs. A user's own provider account or API key can be connected without a JetBrains AI subscription and does not consume JetBrains AI credits.

free_tier.stated: The Student Pack is quoted as '10 JetBrains IDEs - the full versions of IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm, plus GoLand, PhpStorm, and others' plus a 'JetBrains AI Pro trial', verified by 'your university email address, ISIC/ITIC card, or GitHub Student Developer Pack', and 'Once your account is verified, you'll receive a pack valid for one year'. Beside it, and needing no verification: 'For students who only need one IDE for a class, a personal project, or the language they're learning - no student verification required', naming IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, CLion, WebStorm, RustRover, Rider, RubyMine and DataGrip.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The ISIC route is the interesting one because it sounds like an international card anyone can buy; the ISIC issuer's own help centre closes it, since the card itself demands dated proof of full-time enrollment. That makes the four JetBrains routes one gate, not four.
record.limits_note: No compute is involved, so no technical quota binds; the only bound is that the full pack needs enrollment proof while the one-IDE routes need nothing and give less.
record.binding_note: No compute is involved, so no technical quota binds; the only bound is that the full pack needs enrollment proof while the one-IDE routes need nothing and give less.

identity_cost.detail: student status, by one of four routes the application form lists: "University email address", "ISIC/ITIC membership", "Official document" or "GitHub". The ISIC route is not a bypass, because the card is "only available to full time students", who must prove current full-time study by student ID card or a signed and dated letter on official stationery. No card, phone, hold or payment is stated, and the pack is "valid for one year" with annual renewal; the one-IDE licences need "no student verification required" but carry no compute

evidence.proved: 'Verify your student status with your university email address, ISIC/ITIC card, or GitHub Student Developer Pack'; one-IDE options say 'no student verification required'; the pack is 'valid for one year' and renewed annually.
The application form offers exactly four verification routes: 'University email address', 'ISIC/ITIC membership', 'Official document', 'GitHub'.

The ISIC card is not an alternative to enrollment proof: 'The ISIC is only available to full time students, so you must be able to prove you are currently studying full time at school, college or university', by student ID card or 'a signed and dated letter on official university or school stationery'.

record.notes: Refutation of a specific hypothesis: ISIC is not a bypass. Worth keeping because earlier readings and every student-offer list treats 'ISIC cards accepted' as if it widened eligibility. It narrows nothing. The non-commercial IDE licence is genuinely reachable and genuinely irrelevant to compute. The JetBrains AI Pro trial is the only part with any inference value, and it is a trial.
